source_text:
Καὶ τὰ μὲν παιδία ἐκ τοῦ αἵματός εἰσι θερμὰ καὶ
ὑγρά· οἱ δὲ νεανίσκοι ἐκ τῆς ξανθῆς χολῆς, θερμοὶ καὶ ξηροί· οἱ δὲ τέλειοι τῇ ἡλικίᾳ

ἀπὸ τῆς μελαίνης χολῆς εἰσὶ ψυχροὶ καὶ ξηροί· οἱ δὲ γέροντες, ἐκ τοῦ φλέγματος εἰσὶ
ψυχροὶ καὶ ὑγροί. Ὁ δὲ κρόταφος οὖν τῆς κεφαλῆς ἐστὶν ὁ ἡγεμὼν τοῦ σώματος· καὶ
ὅσον ὁ ἐγκέφαλος εὐκατασταθείη καὶ ὑγιαίνοι, καὶ ὅλα τὰ μέλη τοῦ σώματος μετ'
εἰρήνης εἰσίν· ἡ δύναμις δὲ καὶ ἡ φρόνησις ἐκ τοῦ ἥπατος ἀναπέμπεται τῷ
ἐγκεφάλῳ, καὶ αὐτὴ ἡ ψυχὴ ἐκεῖ ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ βυθὸς τῶν νοημάτων. Ἔχει δὲ ἡ
κεφαλὴ ῥαφὰς πέντε· ἔστι δὲ καὶ κεφαλὴ μονόῤῥαφος, καὶ ἔστιν αὐτὴ πάντοτε ὑγιής.
Ὁ δὲ ἐγκέφαλος ἔχει μήνιγγας τρεῖς· ὁ μὲν πρῶτος ὑποζωματίας· ὁ δὲ δεύτερος,
χαρακοειδής· ὁ δὲ τρίτος, ....τοειδής. Τοῦ δὲ ἐγκεφάλου εἰσὶ μέρη τρία· ὁ μὲν εἷς,
κυρεβοειδής· ὁ δεύτερος, ὁ θίτος, καὶ ὁ τρίτος νοερός. Ἔστι δὲ οὐσία θερμώδης.
thought_title: Humors, the head's rule, and the brain's parts
orientation: John of Damascus continues his account of the four humors, now linking each to a stage of life and its qualities, then turns to the head as ruler of the body and describes the brain's sutures, membranes, and parts.
pass_a_gloss: And the children from the blood are warm and moist; and the young men from the yellow bile, warm and dry; and the perfect in age from the black bile are cold and dry; and the old men, from the phlegm are cold and moist. And the temple of the head therefore is the ruler of the body; and as much as the brain would be well settled and would be healthy, also all the members of the body are with peace; and the power and the thought from the liver is sent up to the brain, and the soul itself is there, and the depth of the thoughts. And the head has five sutures; and there is also a single-sutured head, and it is always healthy. And the brain has three membranes; the first, hypozomatias; and the second, charakoeides; and the third, ....oeides. And of the brain there are three parts; the one, kyreboeides; the second, the thitos, and the third noeros. And it is a warm substance.

choices.why: Keeps the literal adjective 'perfect' with the dative of respect 'in age', matching the source's word order and not smoothing into 'adults'.
Renders the optative as a condition ('as much as... would be') and keeps the compound sense of being well established, not just 'healthy'.
Literal rendering of 'depth' with the plural genitive 'of the thoughts', preserving the spatial metaphor.
Keeps the compound adjective as a hyphenated English compound, matching the source's single word.
Transliterated because it is a technical anatomical term with no clear English equivalent; the literal lane keeps the source form rather than guessing.
Renders 'ousia' as 'substance' and the adjective 'thermōdēs' as 'warm', keeping the predicate position.

pass_b_english: Children, then, are warm and moist because of blood. Young men are warm and dry because of yellow bile. Those who are full-grown in age are cold and dry because of black bile. Old men are cold and moist because of phlegm. The temple, then, is the ruler of the body. As long as the brain is well settled and healthy, all the limbs of the body are at peace. Power and thought are sent up to the brain from the liver, and the soul itself is there, along with the depth of thoughts. The head has five sutures. There is also a single-sutured head, and it is always healthy. The brain has three membranes: the first is hypozomatias, the second is charakoeides, and the third is ...oeides. The brain has three parts: one is kyreboeides, the second is the thitos, and the third is noeros. It is a warm substance.
notes: The third membrane name is damaged in the source: '....τοειδής' has missing letters before 'τοειδής'. The gloss preserves the damage as '....oeides' without inventing text.

problems.why: glossary: banned rendering 'temple of the head' (use 'temple')
lint glossary: banned rendering of κρόταφος; use 'temple' ('temple of the head')

edits.old: The temple of the head, then, is the ruler of the body.
edits.new: The temple, then, is the ruler of the body.

fixed: Replaced 'temple of the head' with 'temple' to comply with the glossary ban on 'temple of the head'.

last_rejected.source_quote: ἡ δύναμις δὲ καὶ ἡ φρόνησις
last_rejected.why: φρόνησις means 'prudence/understanding', not 'thought' which renders νοῦς.
last_rejected.fix: Power and prudence are sent up to the brain from the liver.
last_rejected.ruling: φρόνησις can mean 'thought/intelligence'; 'thought' is within normal range, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: οὐσία means 'essence/substance' but θερμώδης means 'warm-like/warmish', not simply 'warm'.
last_rejected.ruling: θερμώδης means 'warmish/warm-like'; 'warm substance' captures οὐσία adequately; minor nuance, not major.
